comments_text: Discovery: identified through sequence homology analysis. This is very close to natural AMPs. The only uncertainty remains in the cleavage site. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that the sequence of this peptide most resembles (46.7% similarity) Chicken CATH-3. Mol Wt: 2623.235; mol formula:C127H204N38O23; GRAVY: -0.53. Activity: Active against Gram- bacteria E. coli ATCC25922 or UB1005 (MIC 2 uM), S. typhimurium ATCC14028 (MIC 4 uM), S. pullorum C79-13 (MIC 8 uM), Gram+ S. aureus ATCC29213 (MIC 4 uM), S. epidermidis ATCC12228 (MIC 4 uM), E. faecalis ATCC29212 (MIC 4 uM), and B. subtilis CMCC63501 (MIC 8 uM). MOA:bacteria:E. coli: depolarized membranes. Structure: random coill in PBS, helical in 30 mM SDS or 50% TFE. In vitro toxicity: human RBC: highly hemolytic: the peptide displayed 50% hemolysis at 8-20 uM (no serum) and 32 uM in the presence of 10% fetal calf serum (FBS). SAR: Two fragments dCATH(1-16) and dCATH(5-20) showed broad activity against both Gram+ and Gram- pathogens (MIC 2-8 uM) in the presence of physiolocal concentrations of salts. These fragments are less toxic. A change of W4 to A, or W17 to A substantially reduced peptide activities. The fragments bind LPS and suppress the release of TNF-alpha, IL-6, and NO from RAW 264.7 cells, implying an anti-inflammatory effect ( Feng et al., 2020). Updated 5/2020; 10/2022; 9/2025
